prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry of a narrow hallway and doorway, showing the camera wearer facing a nearby wall or door (~0.5 m away, within arm's reach) in frame 1 before turning and advancing down a dark corridor (~3 to 4 m deep) through frames 2 to 5. Bright side surfaces in frames 2 to 4 indicate flanking walls and doorframes within 0.5 to 1 m to the left and right of the wearer, while the recessed doorway and far end of the hall appear dark at roughly 2.5 to 4 m ahead. In frame 5, as the wearer moves closer (~1.5 to 2 m from the far white door) and turns slightly left, the near-field bright wall on the right passes out of view and the overall depth gradient flattens into mid-grey tones. Compared to the dim RGB strip, the depth map clarifies the continuous receding planes of the side walls and doorway edges, though it is unreliable inside the dark hallway in frames 2 to 4 where the person standing ~2.5 to 3.5 m ahead is completely absorbed into the black background depth, and in frame 5 where per-frame scale normalization makes the closer wall appear darker than the nearer walls in earlier frames.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates a single person standing in the dark hallway in frames 3 and 4 at roughly 2.5 to 3.5 m in front of the camera wearer, well beyond arm's reach, while leaving all architectural surfaces (walls, doorframes, and the far door ~3 to 4 m away) unlabelled in black. In frame 3, the person is centred in the corridor facing away from the camera wearer (back of the patterned hoodie visible in RGB), and in frame 4 the mask shifts slightly up and to the left as the wearer advances and the person approaches the far doorway (~0.5 m in front of the white door). The map makes the silhouette and vertical extent of the person in the shadowed corridor much easier to separate from the dark background than in the underexposed RGB frames. However, it is unreliable across time and lighting: it completely misses the person in frame 2 (deep in shadow) and frame 5 (where the person is partly occluded by the left doorframe wall edge), and in frame 3 it erroneously splits the single person into two overlapping masks (an upper brown torso mask and a lower pink full-body mask) with the feet clipped at the bottom edge.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons for either the camera wearer or the person ahead in the hallway. From the RGB and other maps, a person is present ~2.5 to 3.5 m ahead in the corridor—facing away from the camera wearer in frame 3, standing near the far white door in frame 4, and partly occluded on the left in frame 5 while the camera wearer's own head shadow appears on the lower part of the far door (~1.5 to 2 m away)—whilst the flanking walls and doorframes remain within ~0.5 to 1 m of the wearer. Because no yellow body or magenta hand keypoints are rendered anywhere in the strip, the pose map adds no visibility over the RGB image and cannot independently establish body orientation, gaze direction, or whether any objects or doors are within arm's reach of the other person. It is completely unreliable in this scene due to the severe low-light conditions in the corridor and the dark silhouette of the person blending into the shadows.
